frontMatter.title: Phase 04 evidence: early real paired execution slice

summary: Phase 04 built the real-pair harness, the broker dispatch bridge with its durable decision-to-effect ledger, the one qualified synthetic harness route, and the early-pair tests, all on feature/mega-maestro-v1.1.0-rc in the Maestro checkout (macOS, Darwin 27, Node v26.12.0). The real pair was exercised inside a Linux container against the sibling endpoint built from its development checkout: the native peer module built there, the daemon started, Maestro's real client and the built library spoke to it, and every answer was the daemon's own refusal because it holds no enrollment. That is not a pair: MRC-04-05 stays unchecked, with CP-01, CP-02 and the registration approval producer named below. No double, no fabricated lease and no dirty-source artifact was counted toward it.
lineBudgetNotes: MRC-04-01 (864), MRC-04-02 (881) and MRC-04-04 (759) are over the 500-line guideline; in each the source files are inside it (the harness script 668 lines, dispatch.ts 331 at MRC-04-02, early-pair.test.ts 380) and the overage is the test or fixture authored in the same task rather than left unexercised. MRC-04-02 touched five source files: the two one-line wirings outside its three named files (the operation attribution in run-agent-turn.ts, the composition in service.ts) are recorded as the bounded continuation MRC-04-02A in the same commit.

realEndpointAttempt.whatThisProves: On Linux, with the native peer module built, the real daemon accepts the real client's framing over its private Unix socket and answers inside the envelope with its own refusals; the built library derives the installation identity the endpoint's identifier rule accepts; the adapter asks nothing of an endpoint it has no registered standing with and answers unavailable; the client refuses to send an operation on an unattached connection; the daemon's control socket answers status and stop. Compared with phase 03 on macOS, the platform refusal (IPC_PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED) is gone: the refusal is now the daemon's unenrolled state (the development peer authority reads no enrollment binding and answers IPC_UNENROLLED, so every runtime peer is unauthenticated and no challenge opens).
realEndpointAttempt.whatThisDoesNotProve: Enrollment, registration, policy delivery, a decision, a receipt, a lease, an effect. The daemon holds no enrollment because no Mega-Maestro API exists to enroll it against or to approve an actor registration; the harness takes approval only from --approve-command and had none. The endpoint source is dirty, so even a complete exchange could not be pinned or certified (CP-01). The sibling runtime adapter still declares itself unsupported (CP-02). The endpoint's broker, by its own code (createExecutionRuntime.withExecution hands the broker null; managedBackendCapability is unsupported; the synthetic-node provider is harness-only), denies every execution request today, so the protected-effects row cannot pass against it until the Mega-Maestro owner qualifies a backend and provider route.

deterministicCoverage.against: the fake daemon (src/__tests__/main/enterprise/fakeEndpoint.ts, a declared double of the socket protocol) with the real client, the real host adapter, the real dispatch bridge and the real startTurn sink; the program is the declared harmless double under the Node permission model
cases: allow: one file in the private work directory, the loopback observer heard no connection, no child started, declared read succeeded, undeclared read refused, wire request in the broker vocabulary with no arguments, ledger released with the observed pid
policy receipt: the broker decision on the lease, joined in the ledger by decision id, with the registration that held
deny before effect: policy_denied, a replay of a consumed request (idempotency-conflict), an endpoint with no execution (unavailable): nothing in any work directory
changed inputs: a lease admitted for one snapshot refuses the spawn of another (snapshot-mismatch) before any effect, lease stays issued
wrong runtime: a context naming another runtime is refused by the verifier; another runtime id cannot attach on the registered socket; the dispatch is unavailable
offline and restart: a dropped endpoint session is unavailable (no request sent) until re-attached on the surviving registration; a second host over the same ledger reads the released receipt
endpoint loss: an answer lost after the request left is unknown; a closed endpoint is unavailable; nothing runs either way
deterministicCoverage.independentObservation: the effects file read from disk by the test, a TCP listener owned by the test counting connections, the work directory listing, and the ledger file read from disk; never the program's stdout alone

builtByEnforcementProperty.property: The broker is spoken to in its own vocabulary and never handed an override
builtByEnforcementProperty.how: operation start/input/resume from the snapshot, no arguments on the wire, resources and policy revision bound; the resolved command line stays in the local lease digest

builtByEnforcementProperty.property: A decision is a decision, an outage is an outage
builtByEnforcementProperty.how: policy_denied, budget_exhausted, unknown_price, untrusted_clock, expired, owner_unfenced deny with policy-denied; replay denies with idempotency-conflict; every other refusal is unavailable; a receipt whose identifiers are not the contract's is unknown

builtByEnforcementProperty.property: The broker's receipt rides the lease and joins its ledger
builtByEnforcementProperty.how: decisionId, requestDigest, brokerId, policyRevision on the lease and the admitted outcome; the ledger joins them to the lease, the registration, the pid and the exit; byDecision() joins back

builtByEnforcementProperty.property: Never authorize, then spawn something else
builtByEnforcementProperty.how: the admitted snapshot's lease is re-checked by digest the instant before spawn; a changed spec throws DispatchRefusedError before any effect (early-pair test, changed inputs)

builtByEnforcementProperty.property: The effect lifetime is written as it happens, and a restart admits ignorance
builtByEnforcementProperty.how: bound with pid, released with exit, revoked with reason; a receipt still live at the last exit is unknown after load; flush() makes the ledger durable before an outcome is returned

builtByEnforcementProperty.property: The synthetic route constrains files and egress by the runtime, not by the program's manners
builtByEnforcementProperty.how: node --permission with --allow-fs-read per declared input and --allow-fs-write for the work directory only; network, child processes, workers, addons and undeclared reads refused with ERR_ACCESS_DENIED; complete environment (PATH, HOME)
one provider on one route id, enforcement per effect, unsupported on Windows or a Node without the flags, doesNotQualify names real providers, descendants and the permission model as an OS boundary

builtByEnforcementProperty.property: The harness names what it cannot prove
builtByEnforcementProperty.how: each missing producer by coordination id and owner; dirty or stale inputs run only with an explicit flag and are recorded certifiable false with the reason; approval only from --approve-command
